title: Private upgrade safelist manager and idempotent migration harness
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private (VPC/on‑prem) customers require near‑zero‑risk upgrades across heterogeneous environments. Existing migration tooling handles schema migrations and rolling pods, but we still observe: nondeterministic partial-migrations, non-idempotent steps that require manual intervention, and insufficient preflight safelists for blocked features.

Goal: Build a migration harness + safelist manager that guarantees idempotent migration steps, coordinates transactional state transfer between control-plane and data-plane components, and provides a per-customer safelist for allowing incremental feature enablement post-upgrade. The harness should be compatible with Helm-based on‑prem installs and our Private agent, and expose rollout gates for Console-driven canaries and automated telemetry gates.

Scope:
- Migration harness that executes named, versioned, idempotent migration tasks with checkpointing and at-least-once semantics but deterministic replay.
- Safelist manager service (configurable per-customer) that can mark resources/features as blocked/allowed during rollout and be enforced by agents.
- Integration with existing rollout gates (canary percentage, error budget, latency regressions) and ability to pause/resume at named gates.
- Preflight validators + dry-run mode that simulate migrations with a shadow state store and emit compatibility reports.
- Runbook + automated rollback and selective step compensation primitives.

Out of scope: automated data model conversions that require manual mapping (these will be surfaced as operator tasks), and migration heuristics tied to third-party DB engines beyond our supported list.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent migration tasks are implemented and can be retried without side-effects
Safelist API allows Console to set per-customer block/allow lists and changes propagate to agents within 30s in typical VPC setup
Migration harness supports dry-run and produces a deterministic compatibility report matching production dry-runs within 5% variance
Canary gate hooks (10%, 50%, 100%) integrate with existing rollout controller and honor pause/resume commands
Automated rollback path documented and exercised in a staging dry-run; runbook validated by SRE and Support
Telemetry emits migration-step-level traces and metrics; alert rules created for step failures and high rollback rates
rollout_plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests 2) Integration test using onprem-staging (helm chart v2026.02) 3) Dry-run across 3 representative customer snapshots 4) Canary rollout via Console: enable for internal tenants (10%), monitor 24h, promote to 50% then 100% 5) Post-cutover telemetry validation and 7‑day stability window
rollback_plan: Each migration step must register a compensating action. The harness supports stepwise rollback: on failure, pause at gate, invoke compensating actions for completed steps in reverse order, verify state via validation hooks. If compensating fails, escalate to manual runbook and pin customers to previous release channel (LTS) until incident resolved.
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: migration.step.duration per-customer and per-step (alert on p99 > threshold)
Metric: migration.step.failure_count (alert on >5 failures across customers in 1h)
Trace: end-to-end migration trace ID linking harness, agent, and DB ops
Console dashboard: per-release and per-customer migration health with safelist overrides visible
Pager: SRE on-call for any rollback escalation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Non-idempotent third-party DB migrations cause inconsistency — Mitigation: require explicit compensating script and mark as manual step in harness
Risk: Safelist propagation delay in high-latency private networks — Mitigation: fallback to local agent enforcement with backoff and audit logs
Risk: Operator error when approving canaries — Mitigation: add pre-approve checks and enforce two-person approval for >50% canaries
Risk: Overlapping concurrent upgrades across multiple clusters — Mitigation: add global cohort leases and per-customer concurrency throttles
implementation_notes: Use existing orchestration layer (release-controller) as the control loop; add migration-step CRD with version and status fields
Store checkpoints in encrypted per-customer namespace in control-plane DB; keep only last 3 checkpoints to limit retention
Safelist manager will expose gRPC + REST endpoints; agents must cache and enforce entries with TTL and checksum validation
Dry-run will use a shadow state store to avoid touching production DBs; snapshot + replay strategy documented in design doc
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Initial design review with Release Eng, SRE, and Platform teams — agreed on idempotent step contract and checkpoint format
2026-02-22: Spike completed for checkpointing prototype; proof-of-concept stores checkpoints and replays steps deterministically (repo: rw-private/upgrade-harness-spike)
2026-03-02: PR #1234 opened implementing safelist service schema and agent cache invalidation protocol — awaiting API review
2026-03-08: Integration tests scheduled against onprem-staging cluster; blocked by helm chart 2026.02 image promotion (ENG-61234) — workaround: use pre-release images
2026-03-12: Console hooks for pause/resume implemented; PM and Support ran first dry-run and provided feedback on runbook clarity
reviews_and_feedback: PM (Liam O'Connor): requested clearer visibility in Console for safelist decisions and a way to annotate why a customer is blocked
SRE (Maya Chen): suggested adding proactive drift detection to preflight validators to catch schema drift between agent and control-plane
Security (Oliver Grant): requested threat model for safelist API and KMS usage for checkpoint storage — security review scheduled
Design (Rosa Park): emphasized UX for canary pause/resume and explicit toasts for operators when safelist blocks requests
next_steps: Address API review comments on PR #1234 and merge safelist schema
Complete integration tests in onprem-staging and iterate on compensating action DSL
Execute a dry-run against 3 customer snapshots and collect compatibility reports
Schedule security review and formal sign-off from SRE and Support before canary
notes: Decision: We will implement compensating actions as script-backed tasks declared alongside migration steps to keep harness language-agnostic
Trade-off: Checkpointing frequency increases storage and latency but reduces rollback work — chosen conservative default of checkpoint per major step
Follow-up: Add per-step cost estimation to help Sales/Customer Success plan upgrade windows for large customers
